newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs to power ahead, challenge 129.25.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs to power ahead, challenge 129.25.

text.p: BTPs will push higher on Thursday to challenge trendline resistance at 129.25, technical analysts said.
And if the market holds above that level at the close, it has the potential to move up towards 130.80, then 131.04 with a new contract high above 131.76 on the cards, they added.
"The whole structure of the market looks pretty constructive here," said Chase technical analyst Guenter Redeker.
"It looks like we may have established a corrective bottom at 123.60 and have entered a fifth Elliott wave up. If that is correct, we will certainly see a new contract high."
By 0812 GMT, June BTPs were up 37 basis points at 128.89, just off an earlier high of 129.05 -- mild resistance from a daily high on April 15.

"If it breaks that, it will challenge trendline resistance at 129.25," said Redeker. "A break of that level confirmed by a daily closing price above here would certainly mean we will test 130.80 ahead of 131.04."
Charts show the market hit a daily high of 131.04 on February 10.
"If we get above 131.04 then it would move towards...the contract high on January 23," Redeker added.
Redeker said the market outlook would weaken if it went below Wednesday's low of 128.26. Below there minor Elliott support at 128.08 would kick in, followed by trendline support at 127.76.
Analysts at a European bank here were more pessimistic on the outlook for BTPs.
"The intraday picture displays activity that could be implying an end to the current run soon -- so watch out," they said. "127.00 looks to be a better buy than 129.00."
By 0824 GMT, June Eurolira was up four basis points at 93.26.
